A typical residential rooftop PV net-metering job falls in Level 1: export capacity ≤25 kW and nameplate ≤50 kW = $50 flat. Level 2 and Level 3 are size-scaled add-on rates ($100 + $1.00/kVA and $500 + $2.00/kVA respectively), so the feeUsd shown for those brackets is the base charge only — the per-kVA adder must be added; Level 4 appears in the guidelines' level list but no fee amount is printed in this table. finding.notes: No utility application/interconnection fee for a residential Pacific Power (PacifiCorp) net-metering application in Oregon. Pacific Power's Oregon net metering is offered under Schedule 135 in compliance with ORS 757.300 and OAR 860-039-0005 through -0080; Schedule 135 itself contains no application or interconnection fee line (searched the tariff PDF for 'fee' — only occurrences are 'feeder' and the 10-foot disconnect-switch language). The controlling fee provision is OAR 860-039-0045 on the Oregon Secretary of State's official OARD site (secure.sos.state.or.us, a .us state domain): Tier 1 = no fee. A residential rooftop PV system is inverter-based and, per OAR 860-039-0030(1), qualifies for Tier 1 if generation capacity is 50 kW or less and export capacity 25 kW or less — which covers essentially every residential job (Oregon's residential net metering cap is 25 kW anyway). CAUTION on the larger/odd cases, where a fee DOES exist: Tier 2 review may be charged up to $50.00 plus $1.00 per kW of facility capacity plus reasonable minor-modification/additional-review costs (engineering not to exceed $100/hr, CPI-adjustable each January); Tier 4 review may be charged up to $100.00 plus $2.00 per kW plus actual impact/facilities study time. Also, if a Tier 1 application is denied and resubmitted under another review procedure, the utility may then impose a fee. SUPERSESSION: the current OARD text (amended by PUC 3-2024, filed/effective 04/09/2024) uses TIER 1/2/4 terminology; the widely-mirrored oregon.public.law copy of 860-039-0045 still shows the older LEVEL 1/2/3 wording with the same dollar amounts — I used the official SOS version. Pacific Power's own multi-state interconnection brochure only says to submit an 'application fee, if required for your state', which is not an Oregon number and should not be relied on. finding.notes: This is Portland General Electric's own published customer documentation (PGE-hosted 'Net Metering • Frequently Asked Questions' PDF, file dated 11.20.25 — the most recent version of that FAQ; an older undated copy of the same FAQ exists on PGE's asset host and says the same thing using the older 'Level 3' wording). Residential net-metering interconnection applications for systems 25 kW or less carry NO PGE application fee, so there is nothing to pay at submission. Two contingencies a coordinator must know: (1) if local grid conditions require a study, PGE will ask for a Tier 4 (formerly Level 3) application, whose fee is $100 plus $2 per kW, with any System Impact Study or Facilities Study billed at $100/hour — PGE, p.1: 'The base fee is $100 plus $2 per kW. Should an application require a System Impact Study or Facilities Study, the study is billed at $100 per hour.'; (2) any required PGE system upgrades are at the customer's expense. Commercial/industrial systems 25 kW–2 MW pay $50 plus $1 per kW — that bracket is NOT applicable to a residential application. These amounts mirror the OPUC caps in OAR 860-039-0045 (Level 1 review: no application fee; Level 2: up to $50 + $1/kW; Level 3: up to $100 + $2/kW), which is the state rule PGE operates under, not a separate charge. Applications are filed through PGE's PowerClerk portal (https://pgenm.powerclerk.com) — the seeded portal URL is consistent with PGE's own instructions ('sends us a completed application through PowerClerk').
